evidence: Graesse, Orbis Latinus (1861), index s.v. Burgas: Bergula
Graesse, Orbis Latinus s.v. Bergulae: Bergulae, Virgulae, Arkadiopolis, Burgas, St., Türkei (Ostrumelien)
terms.comment: Graesse’s entry, which the 1861 index printed as Bergula. Graesse equates the place with Arkadiopolis; we have not confirmed the identification in another source, and it may belong to another Thracian town called Burgas. We have found no other Latin name for the Bulgarian port. A town takes no preposition: Bergulās (to), Bergulīs (in, at, from).

sources: J. G. Th. Graesse, Orbis Latinus, edition of F. Benedict (1909), Latin–German, read in the digitization at columbia.edu (cited as Graesse, Orbis Latinus s.v.); its forms are post-classical unless Lewis & Short has them.
J. G. Th. Graesse, Orbis Latinus (Dresden, 1861), German–Latin index, read in the scan at archive.org; cited only where it differs from the 1909 edition.
